week_notes: Side leans went 21-28-2 and total leans 27-24. Taking out games that chance decided, the sides were 16-24-2 (9 to chance) and the totals 21-17 (13 to chance). The 34 staked bets went 13-19-2 (-7.18 units).

Average miss: on the margin the model 15.49 and the market 13.51; on the total the model 12.15 and the market 11.65. It was the model's worst week of the season on margins. Where it sat far from the market (SAC @ EMU by 16, TOL @ MSU by 15, WKU @ NEV), the market was usually right.

Biggest real misses: WKU @ NEV (NEV 49-14 on a pick'em, model off by 44.5), MASS 37-21 at RUTG as a 29.5-point underdog with 5 RUTG turnovers, CLEM @ LSU (off by 35.6), and TXST @ TEX and M-OH @ PITT (both off by about 30).

Chance decided 20 of 51 games. Garbage time settled several results, among them the BALL @ OSU side and total, the OHIO @ NEB and MOST @ TA&M sides, and the SJSU @ USC, MASS @ RUTG, CCU @ WVU, UNT @ IU and KENT @ SC totals. A few draft verdicts that blamed chance on a quarterback exit were moved back to the merits: the quarterback who left was a backup, or the game was already settled.

The week-1 board was rebuilt later (backfilled), and its player projections came from last season's rosters. Nearly every game projects quarterbacks and backs who had left, and some transfers are projected for two teams (Bryson Washington for AUB and BAY, Trent Walker for ORST and HOU). The player scorecard for this week (302 of 596 met) should be read with that in mind. Candidate checks: a week-1 roster refresh after transfers, and pulling week-1 margins toward the market when the model sits 7+ points away. Both are tests to set up under the keep rule, not changes.

2026_01_UNC_TCU.headline: UNC won 15-10 on a neutral field. The UNC +7.5 lean won on the merits, but the over lost badly: 25 points against a 46.5 line, and the model and market both missed by about 22.
right: UNC +7.5 won outright. The model had TCU by 4.7 and the market TCU by 7.5; the model was closer (off by 9.7 against 12.5).
UNC's offense was more efficient (45.6% success against 36.6%).
wrong: The over 46.5 (model 47.3) lost by 21.5. Neither team scored after UNC's field goal at 10:04 of the third quarter.
TCU went 1 TD in 10 drives, with 3 turnovers on downs. UNC lost 2 fumbles and missed a field goal.
Jeremy Scott (WR, TCU) had 3 yards on 4 targets against 35 projected. Major Everhart (WR, TCU) had no targets.
chance: Little chance here: fumble bounces and a short missed field goal moved the margin about 4.5 points. That doesn't flip either lean.
improve: Both projected quarterbacks, Josh Hoover (TCU) and Gio Lopez (UNC), didn't play. Jaden Craig started for TCU and wasn't projected. The week-1 board projected last year's starters: a data fix to check.
Possibility: new quarterbacks on both sides in an opener, and the scoring dried up. Candidate check: shade week-1 totals down when both starters are new?

2026_01_SJSU_USC.headline: USC led 35-3 after three quarters and won 42-26. SJSU +37.5 covered on the merits. The under was beaten only by 30 garbage-time points.
right: SJSU +37.5 won (the bet too). The model had USC by 30.4, the market by 37.5; the model was 7 points closer.
Even without the fourth-quarter points, USC led by 32 after three quarters, short of 37.5.
wrong: USC's offense was close to perfect: 6 TDs on 10 drives, 6 of 7 red-zone trips, 67.9% success.
chance: The under 61 was decided by garbage time: SJSU scored 23 and USC 7 in the fourth with USC up 17+. The total was 38 after three quarters and went over at 1:45 of the fourth.
improve: Projected Xavier Ward (QB, SJSU) and Danny Scudero (WR, SJSU) didn't play; Scudero turned up at COLO. Transfers weren't on the week-1 board.
Possibility: SJSU's backups ran up the score late against USC's backups. A total test that treats garbage-time points as noise has come up before.

2026_01_NCSU_UVA.headline: UVA rolled 34-8. Both leans lost on the merits: the model had a close game, and NCSU's offense managed 0.67 points a drive.
right: Nothing went right for the leans here.
wrong: NCSU +4 (model UVA by 1.9) lost by 22. UVA led 10-0 in the first quarter and was never caught.
The over 50.5 (model 53) lost: 42 points. NCSU scored only 8, on 1 TD in 12 drives with 2 turnovers.
CJ Bailey (QB, NCSU) threw for 84 yards on 23 attempts (3.7 a throw) against 218 projected. NCSU trailed by 9+ on 84% of its plays.
Victor Snow (WR, NCSU) had 5 yards on 2 targets against 47 projected. Jayden Scott (RB, NCSU) had 20 on 7 carries.
chance: Almost none: fumble bounces were worth about 1.5 points. The result reflects how the teams played.
improve: UVA started Beau Pribula, not the projected Chandler Morris, and UVA's projected backs J'Mari Taylor and Harrison Waylee didn't play. NCSU's Hollywood Smothers didn't play either.
Possibility: UVA converted 4 of 4 fourth downs, an aggressive plan the model couldn't price.
Candidate check: how far week-1 ratings lean on last season when a team changes quarterback.

2026_01_JVST_NDSU.headline: NDSU won 33-7. Both leans lost on the merits. The model's total of 55.7 was 9 points over the market and 15.7 over the result.
right: The market's 46.5 was much closer on the total than the model's 55.7.
wrong: JVST +7 (model NDSU by 4.7) lost by 26. NDSU led 17-7 at halftime and scored on 6 of 11 drives (2 TDs, 4 FGs).
The over 46.5 lost: 40 points. JVST scored 0.7 points a drive and nothing after the first quarter.
Caden Creel (QB, JVST) threw for 85 yards on 23 attempts (3.7 a throw) against 170 projected. Mekhi Collins (WR, NDSU) had 11 yards on 4 targets against 41.
chance: NDSU returned the opening kickoff for a TD. Without it NDSU still wins by about 20, so the side lean loses either way, and the total is lower still.
improve: Cam Cook (RB, JVST), projected for 95 rushing yards, didn't play. Jalen Likely ran for 48 in his place and wasn't projected.
The model's total gap of 9.2 is large for an FCS opponent. Candidate check: how the model rates FCS teams (NDSU) in week 1 before any games.

2026_01_SAC_EMU.headline: EMU won 28-17. The model had SAC winning by 6.6, a 16-point gap from the market, and the market was right (off by 1.5 against 17.6).
right: The board blended the model down to EMU by 4.9, which held most of the damage.
wrong: SAC +9.5 lost (the bet too). EMU scored 21 in the second quarter and settled the cover at 14-3.
The over 53 (model 55.6) lost: 45 points. Neither team scored in the third quarter, and SAC managed 1.31 points a drive.
Harold Mack (WR, EMU) had 14 yards on 3 targets against 43 projected; EMU led by 9+ on 57% of its plays.
chance: SAC scored a non-offensive TD, which helped the lean. Taken out, EMU wins by about 19.
improve: A 16-point gap from the market in week 1 is a warning sign. Candidate test: cap the model's weight when it disagrees with the market by 10+ before any games are played.
EMU's projected backs (McMillan, Dunlap) and four projected receivers didn't play. The week-1 board's rosters were stale.

2026_01_HAW_STAN.headline: HAW led 27-23 with four minutes left, then STAN scored twice in 29 seconds to win 37-27. The HAW +5 lean lost late, and the over won on the merits.
right: The over 48.5 (model 51.6) won: 64 points. It went over at 4:06 of the fourth, and it stays over without STAN's non-offensive TD.
HAW scored 20 in the fourth quarter, on 5 TDs in 14 drives for the game.
wrong: HAW +5 (model STAN by 2.4) lost. STAN's TDs at 1:41 and 1:12 of the fourth turned a HAW lead into a 10-point loss.
Cam Barfield (RB, HAW) had 1 carry against 5.4 projected.
chance: STAN scored a non-offensive TD and a safety. Taking out the chance items leaves STAN by about 6, still a cover by a point, so it stays on the merits.
improve: STAN's quarterback was Davis Warren (326 yards), not the projected Elijah Brown, and four STAN receivers who weren't projected had 44-81 yards each.
Possibility: HAW's long trip in week 1 (Honolulu to Palo Alto). A test of travel for HAW is a candidate.

2026_01_NMSU_FSU.headline: FSU won 34-17 but never got close to covering 31. The model and market had almost the same number, so the side loss was a shared miss; the under won.
right: The under 53.5 won: 51 points. It also stays under without NMSU's 7 garbage-time points.
wrong: FSU -31 (model FSU by 31.7, a gap of 0.7) lost. FSU led 24-10 after three quarters and by no more than 17.
Quintrevion Wisner (RB, FSU) had 4 carries against 11.2 projected; Ousmane Kromah ran for 115. Zay Parks had no carries.
chance: No chance items of note. NMSU's 0-for-1 red-zone trip and FSU's 4 of 6 were play, not luck.
improve: FSU's starter was Ashton Daniels; the projected Thomas Castellanos didn't play. Gavin Sawchuk didn't play either.
A 0.7-point gap isn't a real lean. Candidate check: should leans under a point be shown as "no lean" in the review?

2026_01_MEM_UNLV.headline: MEM won 27-21. The MEM +5 lean won on the merits, and the over lost because UNLV stalled in the red zone and nobody scored in the last 12 minutes.
right: MEM +5 won (the bet too). The model had UNLV by 0.7, the market by 5; the model was closer (off by 6.7 against 11).
MEM scored 17 in the third quarter and took the lead for good at 24-21.
wrong: The over 55.5 (model 56.4) lost: 48 points. UNLV scored 1 TD on 4 red-zone trips, missed a short field goal and turned it over on downs twice.
Dallan Hayden (RB, MEM) had 1 carry against 6.7 projected; Manny Covey ran for 46 instead.
chance: Fumble bounces and a short missed field goal roughly cancelled out (0.1 points on the margin).
improve: UNLV started Jackson Arnold, not the projected Anthony Colandrea, and three projected MEM backs didn't play or barely did.
Possibility: a 98-degree night kickoff in week 1 may have slowed both offenses late.

2026_01_MASS_RUTG.headline: MASS, a 29.5-point underdog, won 37-21 at RUTG. Everyone missed this one by more than 40 points; RUTG turned it over 5 times. The over got home only on garbage time.
right: MASS +29.5 won outright. The lean was small (model RUTG by 27.4) and the model was a little closer than the market (43.4 against 45.5).
MASS's defense had 4 interceptions (Jahmad Harmon 2).
wrong: Antwan Raymond (RB, RUTG) ran for 42 on 14 carries (3.0 a carry) against 86 projected. Clay Thevenin had 4 on 3 carries. RUTG trailed by 9+ on 71% of its plays.
chance: The over 55 (model 58.1) won only through garbage time. RUTG scored 14 and MASS 3 in the fourth with MASS up 17+, and the over arrived at 1:57.
Fumble bounces went RUTG's way by about 3 points; MASS still wins by about 13 without them.
improve: Neither projected quarterback played: Athan Kaliakmanis (RUTG) and Grant Jordan (MASS). RUTG used Dylan Lonergan and AJ Surace. The week-1 board's quarterbacks were last year's.
Possibility: a 45-point miss in an opener suggests the preseason ratings had RUTG too high or MASS too low. Recheck the week-1 priors for teams with big roster turnover.

2026_01_AKR_WAKE.headline: WAKE led 38-3 early in the fourth and won 38-16. The AKR +27.5 cover and the over both came from garbage-time scores.
right: Before garbage time, the model's WAKE by 19.8 looked short: WAKE led by 35. The fourth-quarter scores pulled it back to 22.
wrong: WAKE was efficient (0.40 EPA a play, 4 TDs and 3 FGs), but it kicked 3 field goals and missed one from close in.
Jordan Gant (RB, AKR) ran for 15 on 8 carries against 67 projected. AKR trailed by 9+ on 93% of its plays.
chance: AKR +27.5 (the bet too) was won by garbage-time TDs at 7:06 and 0:29 of the fourth. Before them WAKE was 35 up, and after the first AKR TD it still led by 28.
The under 50.5 was sunk by the same scores: the total went over at 0:29. AKR scored 13 and WAKE 7 in garbage time.
improve: Both projected quarterbacks didn't play: Robby Ashford (WAKE) and Ben Finley (AKR). WAKE started Gio Lopez; AKR's Cibastian Broughton (193 yards) wasn't projected.
Carlos Hernandez (WR, WAKE) had 165 against 40 projected, and Ty Clark III ran for 105: new roles the week-1 board didn't have.

2026_01_COLO_GT.headline: COLO won 14-13 on a TD with 37 seconds left. GT -6.5 lost on the merits: it scored no red-zone TDs and missed two short field goals. The under won easily.
right: The under 53 won: 27 points, 26 under. The model had 51.7, so the lean was small (gap 1.3).
wrong: GT -6.5 (model GT by 10.8; the bet too) lost. GT went 0 for 3 in the red zone, and its only TD was non-offensive.
Danny Scudero (WR, COLO) had 12 yards on 4 targets against 56 projected. Malachi Hosley (RB, GT) ran for 14 on 6 carries against 38.
chance: The draft marked this chance for Landon Shaffer leaving, but he took 7% of GT's snaps at quarterback; Alberto Mendoza played the game. That isn't a starter's exit.
GT's non-offensive TD and COLO's fumble luck roughly offset (net 1 point). Without them COLO wins by about 2, so the side still loses.
improve: GT's projected starter Haynes King and COLO's Kaidon Salter didn't play. Mendoza wasn't projected; COLO started Julian Lewis.
Possibility: three GT defenders faced COLO, a former team. Lamont Lester Jr. (COLO) had 3 sacks.
Candidate check: GT missed 2 short field goals. Kicker form isn't in the model.

2026_01_UAB_ILL.headline: ILL won 42-23. Both leans won, but both needed garbage time: UAB's TD with 9 seconds left turned a push into a cover, and ILL's late TD took the total over.
right: Both offenses moved the ball: ILL scored 5 TDs in 8 drives, and UAB scored on 6 of 8 (3 TDs, 3 FGs).
The model was closer than the market on the margin (off by 2.9 against 7).
wrong: Nobody was far short of projections in this game.
chance: UAB +26 (the bet too): ILL led 42-16, exactly 26, until UAB scored with 0:09 left. A garbage-time TD turned a push into a win.
The over 54 went over at 5:48 of the fourth on an ILL TD with ILL already up 19. Without the 14 garbage-time points it's 51, under. ILL also had a non-offensive TD.
improve: Neither projected quarterback played: Luke Altmyer (ILL) and Jalen Kitna (UAB). UAB's Rod Robinson II ran for 59 and wasn't projected.

2026_01_SJSU_EMU.headline: SJSU lost Luke Weaver on its first drive and still won 27-21 at EMU. The EMU -1.5 lean and the over both lost on the merits.
right: Little went right. The model and market were close on the margin (1.9 against 1.5).
wrong: EMU -1.5 lost. SJSU's backups scored 4 TDs and 2 FGs; Jabari Bates ran for 119. SJSU went ahead for good at 11:19 of the fourth.
The over 55 (model 57.7) lost: 48 points, including EMU's non-offensive TD. Without it the total is 41.
Noah Kim (QB, EMU) threw 43 times for 174 yards (4.0 a throw) against 241 projected.
chance: The draft marked this chance for Weaver's exit, but losing SJSU's quarterback hurt SJSU, not the EMU lean, and SJSU won anyway. EMU's non-offensive TD helped the lean; without it SJSU wins by about 14.
improve: Projected EMU backs McMillan and Dunlap didn't play again; Amareon Blue (93 yards) wasn't projected. SJSU's projected Scudero, Shoels and two backs didn't play.
Candidate check: a backup quarterback from the first series played well. The board has no read on college backups.

2026_01_UTEP_OU.headline: OU won 51-0 and covered 41 by 10. Chance flipped the UTEP +41 lean: OU's non-offensive TD and UTEP's two short missed field goals were worth about 11 points. The under won.
right: The under 51.5 (model 46.5) won: 51 points, and it stays under without OU's 7 garbage-time points.
OU's offense did what the market expected: 5 TDs and 3 FGs on 11 drives.
wrong: UTEP scored 0. It went 0 for 2 in the red zone, missed 3 field goals and lost 2 fumbles.
Kam Thomas (RB, UTEP) had no targets and Jaden Smith (WR, UTEP) had none caught on 1. UTEP trailed by 9+ on 95% of its plays.
chance: Take out OU's non-offensive TD, UTEP's short missed field goals and the fumble bounces and OU wins by about 40, under 41. Chance decided the side.
improve: UTEP's projected quarterback Skyler Locklear didn't play. EJ Colson Jr. started, and Raymond Moore III wasn't projected.
The model had OU by only 32.2, 9 points under the market. Candidate check: does the model shrink big week-1 mismatches too much?

2026_01_TOL_MSU.headline: MSU won 30-20, exactly the 10-point line. The model had TOL winning by 4.9, a 15-point gap; the market was spot on. The under lost on a field goal at 1:55.
right: TOL +10 pushed (the bet too). TOL even led 20-19 early in the fourth.
wrong: The model's TOL by 4.9 missed by 14.9; the market missed by 0.
The under 48.5 (model 48) lost: 50 points. MSU's field goal at 1:55 took it over, with MSU up 7, so it wasn't garbage time.
Cam Fancher (QB, MSU) had 1 carry against 7 projected: he barely ran.
chance: Little chance: fumble bounces and TOL's short missed field goal were worth about 3 points. MSU wins by about 7 without them, so the push stands on the merits.
improve: TOL's projected quarterback Kalieb Osborne didn't play; John Alan Richter (177 yards) and Adjatay Dabbs (101) weren't projected. Chip Trayanum and Junior Vandeross III didn't play.
As with SAC, a week-1 gap of 15 points from the market went the market's way. Same candidate test: cap the model's weight on big disagreements before any games.

2026_01_MIA_STAN.headline: MIA crushed STAN 45-6. Both leans won, but they were tiny (0.1 on the side, 0.9 on the total), so the model and market had the same game.
right: MIA -24.5 won by 14.5: MIA led 35-6 early in the third.
The over 46.5 won: 51 points, over by the third quarter (5:24). Only 3 garbage-time points.
Darian Mensah (QB, MIA) threw for 401 and Malachi Toney had 234 receiving yards.
wrong: Micah Ford (RB, STAN) ran for 27 on 11 carries against 55 projected. JonAnthony Hall (WR, STAN) had 6 yards on 4 targets. STAN trailed by 9+ on 82% of its plays.
Mark Fletcher Jr. (RB, MIA) ran 13 times for 40 (3.1 a carry) against 69 projected: the yards went through the air.
chance: No chance items: no fumble swings, return TDs or short misses.
improve: A lean of 0.1 points isn't a real opinion. Candidate check: show leans under a point as "no lean" in the review.
Possibility: STAN's second game in six days (it played HAW on Aug 29).

2026_01_FRES_USC.headline: USC shut out FRES 39-0. Both leans won on the merits: USC -22 by 17, and the under by 12.5.
right: USC -22 (model USC by 24.5) won: USC led 30-0 at halftime. The model was closer than the market (14.5 against 17).
The under 51.5 (model 49.3) won: 39 points. FRES had 0 explosive plays and 0 points.
wrong: Josiah Freeman (WR, FRES) had 0 yards on 3 targets against 50 projected. FRES backs Donelson and Luke averaged 2.5 a carry. FRES trailed by 9+ on 67% of its plays.
chance: Fumbles went slightly against the lean (USC lost 2); it didn't matter.
improve: FRES's projected quarterback E.J. Warner didn't play; Jayden Mandal threw for 77. USC's projected Makai Lemon, Ja'Kobi Lane and Eli Sanders missed a second straight game.
USC receivers Trent Mosley (104) and Kayden Dixon-Wyatt (102) weren't projected, though Mosley had 118 the week before. The week-1 board didn't pick up a role from the previous game.

2026_01_ECU_ALA.headline: ALA won by 38 as a 28.5-point favourite, so the ECU +28.5 lean lost on the merits. The under lost by 5.5, but a 7-point non-offensive TD and 10 garbage-time points decided that.
right: The market (ALA by 28.5) and the board (24.7) were much closer than the model (15.4). The market missed by 9.5, the model by 22.6.
wrong: ECU +28.5 lost. ALA scored on 7 of its 11 drives (4.36 points a drive) and led 38-10 after three quarters.
ECU's backs came up short on a script where ECU trailed by 9+ on 93% of its plays: TJ Engleman Jr. had 1 carry for -2 (23 projected), and Ashton Gray had 17 yards on 2.8 a carry (34.8 projected).
chance: ALA's non-offensive TD added 7 points. Without it the game lands at 51, under 52.5.
ALA's 10 fourth-quarter points came while it led by 28+. The total went over on the first of them (Q4 14:57).
improve: The board projected Ty Simpson (ALA) and Katin Houser (ECU), who didn't play. Keelon Russell had 332 yards for ALA and wasn't projected. Possibility: the board's week-1 projections were built from last season's rosters (this week is backfilled), so they listed players who had left. Data check: week-1 rosters after transfers.
Possibility: the model rated ALA too low against a big talent gap (974 to 624). Week-1 ratings lean on last season.

2026_01_ORST_HOU.headline: Both leans won on the merits. ORST +21 covered in a 33-20 loss, and the game went over 50.5 on HOU's last TD with 5:01 left.
right: ORST +21 (model HOU by 16.7) won: HOU by 13. The model missed by 3.7, the market by 8.
Over 50.5 won at 53, with no garbage time. HOU scored on 6 of 11 drives.
wrong: Trent Walker was projected for both ORST (44 yards) and HOU (43 yards) and had 24 on 3 targets. That is one player counted twice.
chance: Little chance either way: no non-offensive TDs and no early exit. ORST went 1 for 5 on fourth down, which kept HOU's margin wider than it looked.
improve: The board projected Tristan Ti'a, not Braden Atkinson (345 yards), and Anthony Hankerson for ORST. Neither projected player played. Possibility: the board's week-1 projections were built from last season's rosters (this week is backfilled), so they listed players who had left. Data check: week-1 rosters after transfers.
Possibility: Walker faced a former team (HOU, 2023-2025). The board listing him on both sides is the data issue to fix.

2026_01_CCU_WVU.headline: CCU +21 covered on the merits: WVU led 24-0 at half, but CCU was inside the number from Q3. The under lost by half a point, and that came only from CCU's garbage-time TDs.
right: CCU +21 (model WVU by 10.8) won: WVU by 7. The model missed by 3.8, the market by 14.
wrong: The total lean was a coin flip (under by 0.1). It lost at 55.
chance: CCU scored 14 points while trailing by 17+ in Q4, then a field goal with 0:27 left took the total over. Without the garbage time it's 41: the under.
improve: The board projected Tad Hudson and Samari Collier for CCU and Scotty Fox Jr. for WVU. None of them played, while Deuce Bailey and Michael Hawkins Jr. started. Possibility: the board's week-1 projections were built from last season's rosters (this week is backfilled), so they listed players who had left. Data check: week-1 rosters after transfers.

2026_01_UNT_IU.headline: UNT +40 covered on the merits in a 52-16 loss. The over 57 also won, but IU's 14 garbage-time points carried it there.
right: UNT +40 (model IU by 25.2) won: IU by 36. That held even with IU scoring 14 points late while up 17+.
wrong: The model's margin missed by 10.8. The market's missed by 4, so the lean won with a number further off than the line.

IU's backs and receivers came up short in a blowout: Lee Beebe Jr. had 33 rushing yards on 14 carries (57.8 projected), and Shazz Preston had 10 yards on 1 target (32.9 projected). IU had only 45 plays.
chance: IU scored its last two TDs (Q4 5:26 and 1:47) while up 29+. Without them the total is 54, under 57.
improve: The board projected Drew Mestemaker for UNT and Fernando Mendoza for IU. Neither played. Possibility: the board's week-1 projections were built from last season's rosters (this week is backfilled), so they listed players who had left. Data check: week-1 rosters after transfers.
Possibility: UNT's Tayven Jackson faced a former team (IU, 2023-2024).

2026_01_OHIO_NEB.headline: OHIO +24 was covering until NEB's last TD, scored while up 21 with 1:53 left. The over won easily: NEB scored 7 TDs on 11 drives.
right: Over 47 (model 50.7) won at 70. It went over early in Q4 (12:05).
wrong: The model's margin (NEB by 11.7) missed by 16.3. The market (NEB by 24) missed by 4.
Nyziah Hunter (NEB) had 17 yards and 0 targets against 32.2 projected. NEB spread the ball to Kwazi Gilmer and Jacory Barney Jr.
chance: NEB's final TD came with a 21-point lead at 1:53, in garbage time. Without it NEB wins by 21 and OHIO +24 covers. OHIO also missed a short field goal.
improve: Jamal Rule had 169 yards for NEB and wasn't projected. The board had Emmett Johnson (88 rushing) and Sieh Bangura for OHIO, and neither played. Possibility: the board's week-1 projections were built from last season's rosters (this week is backfilled), so they listed players who had left. Data check: week-1 rosters after transfers.

2026_01_LIB_JMU.headline: JMU -6 won on the merits, 20-13. JMU's quarterback JC Evans left late in Q3 with JMU up 20-6, so the exit hurt the side that covered anyway. The over 50.5 lost badly: 33 points.
right: JMU -6 (model JMU by 17.3) won by 7. JMU went up 17-3 in Q2 and held on.
wrong: The over (model 51) lost by 17.5. Neither offence moved: LIB went 0 for 2 in the red zone, and JMU's EPA per play was -0.02.
The model's margin of 17.3 was 10.3 too high. The market's 6 missed by 1.
chance: The QB exit came at 20-6 late in Q3. It didn't decide either lean: JMU still covered, and the game was 26 points with a quarter left.
improve: The board projected Alonza Barnett III (JMU) and Michael Merdinger (LIB). Neither played: Deshawn Purdie had 233 yards for LIB. Possibility: the board's week-1 projections were built from last season's rosters (this week is backfilled), so they listed players who had left. Data check: week-1 rosters after transfers.

2026_01_M-OH_PITT.headline: PITT crushed M-OH 59-14, and model and market were both about 29 points off. The M-OH lean lost on the merits, and the over won by 25.5.
right: Over 47.5 (model 48.8) won at 73. It went over early in Q3.
wrong: M-OH +16.5 lost by 28.5. PITT scored 8 TDs on 12 drives, and M-OH's success rate was 26%.
This was one of the week's biggest misses for everyone: model 30.2, market 28.5.
chance: Nothing big: fumbles near even, no non-offensive TDs, no early exit. PITT led 52-14 after three quarters.
improve: Mason Heintschel threw for 453 yards against 229 projected. Possibility: a week-1 rating built on last year's PITT passing game underrated him.

The board projected Thomas Gotkowski, but David McComb played QB for M-OH. Possibility: the board's week-1 projections were built from last season's rosters (this week is backfilled), so they listed players who had left. Data check: week-1 rosters after transfers.

2026_01_BALL_OSU.headline: OSU covered -51 only with a TD at 1:55 while up 46, and the under lost on that same score. Both results came down to garbage time.
right: The model's margin (51.5) was right on: OSU by 53.
wrong: The model's total (45.1) was 10.9 under the line and missed by 13.9. The market missed by 3.
